items.title: Iran-Linked Hackers Abuse Legitimate Developer Tool to Hide Dindoor Backdoor
items.description: Iran-linked operators are using a trusted developer tool to conceal a backdoor called Dindoor inside Windows environments. The malware uses the Deno JavaScript and TypeScript runtime to execute encoded code, helping its activity blend into legitimate software use. items.description: A routine development mistake has exposed thousands of software repositories. items.title: NVIDIA NemoClaw Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack AI Agents With One Website Visit
items.description: A critical vulnerability in NVIDIA NemoClaw that could let attackers hijack an AI agent after a victim visits a malicious website. The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-65105, can expose the local Ollama model server used by NemoClaw and allow persistent poisoning of the AI model’s behavior. items.description: Two serious Microsoft SharePoint Server vulnerabilities can be chained to let remote attackers take control of vulnerable servers without a password. items.title: Multiple OpenSSL Flaws Let Remote Attackers Crash Servers and Corrupt Heap Memory
items.description: OpenSSL has issued a fresh security advisory disclosing seven vulnerabilities across its cryptographic library, ranging from a heap-corrupting write bug to memory-exhaustion flaws in its QUIC and DTLS implementations.
